review.reviewBody: I used to spend hours every week ordering food. Now it's simple, super easy, and I have free time to spend on other aspects of my restaurant.

@graph.name: Adding voice orders beside B2B Wave
@graph.description: It takes three things: your list of each account's usual items, the accounts we open, and our app on each chef's phone.

step.name: List each restaurant's regulars
step.text: Each restaurant's regular products, with prices and your codes, are usually all we need.

step.name: We open each account
step.text: Its guide is loaded and the chef gets the app. Most restaurants send a first order the same day.

step.name: Chefs start saying their orders
step.text: Their orders reach you checked, numbered and timed, while portal accounts carry on as before.

@graph.name: Do I need a B2B Wave alternative for orders that chefs say aloud?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Your portal, customer prices, recurring orders and sales rep tools are untouched. What you add is a second way in for chefs who favor talking: they say it to our app and go over each item before it goes, and nobody at your end has to take a call.

@graph.name: Is VoiceOrder Solutions better than B2B Wave?

acceptedAnswer.text: At one job: taking an order from a chef who is happier speaking than typing, then putting every item in front of that chef to fix on the spot. B2B Wave does far more as a web portal, with quotes, online payment and rep tools, so we stay at its side and are not a B2B Wave alternative.

@graph.name: B2B Wave already makes reordering quick. Why bring in an app?

acceptedAnswer.text: Keep it: for a chef at a screen, reordering there is quick. It still takes typing, tapping or scanning, and some chefs simply prefer saying it. Voice is not ours alone: other firms offer AI calling and messaging tools that connect to B2B Wave. Those handle calls and messages; ours shows the chef each item to fix before sending.

@graph.name: Are the two linked, and does somebody still have to type orders?

acceptedAnswer.text: The two come from separate companies and are not linked, and each one supports just its own software. B2B Wave has an API for creating orders, but nothing connects ours to it today. If your setup can take our orders over EDI or our API, no one types them again; whether it can is something to settle in the demo. Over email, though, each one still has to be entered at your end. What your desk skips is the call itself: nobody listens, notes each item and repeats it back, since every item was gone through on the chef's side first. B2B Wave and the systems behind it keep account details, billing and stock; we keep the guides, with your prices on them, plus every app-placed order. Your system still gives an order its own number once it is entered.

@graph.name: Our reps already put orders in for chefs who call. What changes?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nothing has to. Reps can keep placing orders for accounts that want it, and carry on with visits as they do now. A chef phoning just to read out the usual items can speak them to our app instead and check the list at once, rather than opening a saved order in the portal afterwards.

@graph.name: Do restaurant customers need to download anything?

acceptedAnswer.text: For ours, yes: each chef installs our app. B2B Wave's portal opens in any browser with no install, which is one more reason to keep it for portal regulars.

@graph.name: How quick is setup, and what does it cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: For most distributors, setup takes 24 to 48 hours, and B2B Wave stays exactly as it is. You give us the items each account usually buys, often exported as a spreadsheet. We put those into our admin as guides and set up every restaurant on the app; once the chef downloads it, most are ordering that same day. B2B Wave shows plan prices on its site; we quote per distributor. A B2B Wave replacement would mean shifting every portal customer, standing order and price list to new software, while an app for the chefs who would rather speak asks none of that.

@graph.name: Where do the B2B Wave details on this page come from?

acceptedAnswer.text: Based on b2bwave.com, read 9 November 2026: the homepage, pricing, features and FAQ pages, the wholesalers and food & beverage pages, the sales rep app page, EDI and integrations pages, and three of its blog posts on reorders, ordering workflows and customers who prefer the phone. The AI calling tools came from a search for B2B Wave integrations. If any of this has gone out of date, send us a note and we will correct it.
